mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week rise in RETAIL_REC from -15.6% to -10.3% (5.3 percentage point gain) signals accelerating consumer return to retail venues. This momentum persists over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC to positive or less negative territory relative to the prior four-week mean of -14.75%.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 5.3 points week-on-week in most recent period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below -14.75% or shows negative week-on-week change in 3 of 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Explosive growth in PARKS mobility (44.3% in t-0w, up from 17.3% in t-1w) indicates outdoor activity substitution away from enclosed retail. This substitution effect suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as consumers redirect discretionary time to parks rather than shopping venues.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the prior 28-day mean, or PARKS mobility declines below 30% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility (16.1% in t-0w, up from 8.1% in t-3w) reflects increased essential-goods shopping frequency. Consumers bundling retail-and-recreation purchases with grocery trips amplify RETAIL_REC through co-location effects when grocery demand remains elevated over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM sustains above 12% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM doubled from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 10% in either of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent TRANSIT suppression (ranging -21.4% to -17.6%) indicates ongoing mobility restrictions or low commuter confidence. When transit remains depressed below -15%, RETAIL_REC cannot recover because foot traffic to retail clusters depends on transit access. RETAIL_REC will remain negative over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has not exceeded -17.6% in any of the four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves to above -10% within two weeks, and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises above -5% within four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 3.9% in t-3w to 2.4% in t-0w) signals people leaving home more frequently. Combined with rising RETAIL_REC (+5.3 points week-on-week), this indicates a sustained shift toward out-of-home activity. RETAIL_REC will continue rising over the next four weeks as the home-exit trend persists.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 3.0% while RETAIL_REC rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 1.5 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility rebounds above 3.5% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC reverses to negative week-on-week change.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous surge in PARKS (44.3%) and modest RETAIL_REC recovery (-10.3%) in t-0w reflects spring seasonal effects. Warm weather drives both outdoor recreation and retail foot traffic. This dual-channel seasonal boost sustains RETAIL_REC gains over the next two weeks before potential normalization.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds 35% and RETAIL_REC improves week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:Both PARKS and RETAIL_REC improved in t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below 25% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: Negative WORKPLACES mobility (declining from -8.7% to -11.6%) indicates reduced office occupancy and commuting. This suppresses retail foot traffic from weekday commuter populations. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed over the next four weeks because the commuter-driven retail channel remains inactive.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES deteriorated from -8.7% to -11.6% over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES improves to above -5% within two weeks, and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises above -5% within four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The convergence of three signals—RETAIL_REC recovery (+5.3 points), GROCERY_PHARM surge (+7.0 points), and PARKS explosion (+27 points)—indicates a regime shift toward high out-of-home activity across all categories. This broad-based mobility rebound will sustain RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks as the activity surge becomes self-reinforcing through social and economic feedback.
candidate_trigger: All three proxies show positive week-on-week change simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:All three categories improved in t-0w
regime_hint: broad reopening with multi-sector activity recovery
